literal: He died young; five hundred bolts of condolence silk were given; he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Heng Province.
idiomatic: He died young; five hundred bolts of condolence silk were given, and he was posthumously general who pacifies the distant and Heng inspector.

literal: Prince of Guangling Yu, styled Shufan.
idiomatic: Yu, Prince of Guangling, styled Shufan.

literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed, made Palace Attendant and Grand General Who Campaigns East, and served as Grand Director of the Outer Capital.
idiomatic: In Taihe year 9 he was enfeoffed, made palace attendant and grand general who campaigns east, and grand director of the outer capital.

literal: Yu from youth was clever and intelligent and had a reputation for deciding cases.
idiomatic: From youth Yu was clever and won a name for deciding cases.

literal: Later the three capitals offices were abolished; Yu became Director of the Court of Justice, made General of the Guard, and presided over capital litigation; he had slight reputation.
idiomatic: When the three capital directorates were abolished he became director of the court of justice and general of the guard, heard capital suits, and gained some reputation.

literal: He was transferred to Special Grand Mentor and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and again made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He rose to special grand mentor and left vice director of the Masters of Writing, then junior tutor of the heir and recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When Gaozu was about to campaign south he sent Yu with the staff to pacify the six garrisons, muster their shock cavalry, and the barbarian peoples were settled and pleased.
idiomatic: Before the southern campaign Gaozu sent Yu with the staff to pacify the six garrisons and muster their shock cavalry; the tribes were settled.

literal: [6] On his return he again held the post of Director of the Court of Justice.
idiomatic: [6] On return he again directed the court of justice.

literal: After the imperial carriage had set out, Yu with Grand Commandant Pi remained on guard, was given Bearer of the Staff—the account is in Pi’s biography.
idiomatic: After the emperor marched, Yu and Grand Commandant Pi stayed behind with bearer of the staff—the account is in Pi's biography.

literal: Gaozu was affectionate toward his younger brothers; when he was about to part he could not bear to separate early and ordered Yu to follow as far as Yanmen, then ordered Yu to return.
idiomatic: Gaozu loved his brothers and could not part early; he had Yu follow to Yanmen, then sent him back.

literal: He looked to his proving effective, and therefore bestowed a ruyi scepter to express his heart.
idiomatic: Expecting results, he gave a ruyi scepter as token of his heart.

literal: When the move of the capital was decided, an edict made Yu concurrent Grand Commandant to announce it at the altars of soil and grain.
idiomatic: When the capital move was settled, Yu was made concurrent grand commandant to announce it at the altars.

literal: After the move to the capital, among the northern frontier peoples and barbarians many had not yet understood.
idiomatic: After the move, many on the northern frontier had not yet understood.

literal: Yu pacified and reassured the capital of Dai; inner and outer were orderly, and Gaozu praised him.
idiomatic: Yu pacified the Dai capital; inner and outer were orderly, and Gaozu praised him.

literal: In the spring of the eighteenth year Yu memorialized resigning the Court of Justice; it was not permitted.
idiomatic: In spring of year 18 Yu asked to resign the court of justice; the request was denied.

literal: Yu memorialized: “The outer-examination ordinance states that at each year’s end the provinces and garrisons list the governors’ and prefects’ records of governance.
idiomatic: Yu wrote: "The outer-examination ordinance requires each year-end listing of governors' and prefects' records of rule.

literal: When the second examination comes, according to their grade and rank, promotion and demotion are made manifest.
idiomatic: At the second examination grades fix promotion and demotion.

literal: In the past fifteen years the hundred officials in the capital have all already undergone examination into three grades.
idiomatic: For fifteen years capital officials have already been graded in three ranks.

literal: This year is already the third cycle; though outwardly the completed ordinance exists, the inner ordinance has not been promulgated.
idiomatic: This year completes the third cycle; the outer rule stands, but the inner rule was never issued.

literal: Inner and outer examination in principle ought to be equal.
idiomatic: Inner and outer examination ought to be equal.

literal: Your servant ventures to apply the outer examination as standard to fix the capital officials’ conduct in office.”
idiomatic: I venture to apply the outer examination to fix capital officials' conduct."

literal: An edict said: “Though the inner examination has not been proclaimed, merit has long been evident; therefore the Bright Hall and Monthly Ordinances record the Three Excellencies and great ministers discussing examination and subordinate officials’ governance—the duties are clearly distinguished.
idiomatic: An edict replied: "Though the inner examination was never proclaimed, merit is long evident—the Bright Hall and Monthly Ordinances have the Three Excellencies grade subordinates; duties are clear.

literal: The Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: The Three Excellencies.

literal: (doubt)
idiomatic: (doubt)

literal: The meaning of the Masters of Writing’s three-year palace ranking—within this inner examination it is already clear.
idiomatic: The Masters of Writing's three-year ranking already makes the inner examination clear.

literal: Yet the matter of examination in principle is not light; the method of inquiring into merit ought to concern my hearing—venturing to issue it lightly is especially rash.
idiomatic: Yet examination is no light matter and merit must reach my ear—your hasty move is rash.

literal: The meaning of each examination ought to fall at the year’s end; since you say this year, how can it be at the beginning of spring!
idiomatic: Examinations belong at year-end—how can you begin in spring!

literal: Now it is only the start of summer—wait until after autumn.”
idiomatic: It is only early summer—wait until autumn."

literal: Gaozu at court discussed government affairs and said to Yu: “Moving the capital to Luoyang is a matter that reaches heaven and earth—but your delusion is only that the deep barrier has not yet been opened.
idiomatic: At court Gaozu told Yu: "Moving the capital to Luoyang reaches heaven and earth—your delusion is only that the deep barrier has not opened.

literal: My house has the four seas—coming and going, what difficulty is there?
idiomatic: My house holds the four seas—what difficulty in coming and going?

literal: When I first set out from Luoyang I instructed Yongshou—all thought it was parting.
idiomatic: When I first left Luoyang I instructed Yongshou—all thought it was farewell.

literal: Since returning, matters of allotment everywhere have already differed from the earlier edict.
idiomatic: Since my return, allotments everywhere have already diverged from the earlier edict.

literal: Now undertaking great work—would I waste effort in vain?
idiomatic: Now I undertake great work—would I waste it in vain?

literal: Moreover I have no younger brothers like the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao—how can I idle in ease day after day?
idiomatic: I have no Zhou and Shao among my brothers—how can I idle day after day?

literal: Now I go north on tour; matters of staying behind should match my intent.”
idiomatic: I go north on tour now; what stays behind should match my intent."

literal: Later Gaozu at court addressed the assembled ministers: “The two principles have been opened and humankind lives between them; therefore heaven does not speak and establishes a lord to stand in its place.
idiomatic: Later at court Gaozu told the ministers: "Heaven and earth are opened and humankind lives between; heaven does not speak and sets a lord in its place.

literal: Thus the Documents praise the merit of the three examinations; the Rites speak of the chapter on examination completed.
idiomatic: The Documents praise three examinations; the Rites speak of completed examination.

literal: From emperors and kings downward this way has not been easy.
idiomatic: From kings downward this path has never been easy.

literal: I with meager virtue have rashly borne the great foundation; I think to join the hundred offices in harmonizing the multitude of affairs.
idiomatic: With meager virtue I have borne the great foundation and mean to join the hundred offices in harmonizing affairs.

literal: Yet my knowledge lacks the ability to know men; I cannot make the court free of the reproach of white-eating nor the wilds free of the barb of the recluse Kaopan; night and day I wake and sleep, always bearing fear and caution.
idiomatic: Yet I cannot know men well enough to end the court's charge of freeloading or the wilds' barb of hidden worthies; night and day I wake in fear.

literal: You all are court worthies and state elites; support and correction are entrusted to you—each lead your hearts to display the meaning of examining merit.
idiomatic: You are court worthies and state pillars—lead your hearts and show what examining merit means.

literal: If you depart from loyalty and rectitude the state has its constant punishments; the worthy though distant must be advanced, the unworthy though near must be demoted.”
idiomatic: Depart from loyalty and the state has fixed punishment; advance the worthy though far, demote the unworthy though near."

literal: He turned to Yu and said: “The upper and lower two grades may be made three grades; the middle grade is only one grade.
idiomatic: He turned to Yu: "Upper and lower may become three grades; the middle is only one grade.

literal: The reason is that upper and lower are the categories of demotion and promotion, therefore they display the beauty of the finest thread; the middle keeps to the root—affairs may broadly pass.”
idiomatic: Upper and lower are promotion and demotion and show the finest distinction; the middle keeps the root and may broadly pass."

literal: Yu first presented the Court of Justice’s five bureaus’ investigating officers.
idiomatic: Yu first presented the court of justice's five bureaus' investigating officers.

literal: Gaozu said: “The difficulty of punishment and imprisonment is truly from antiquity; when it comes to deciding litigation, the Master praised it.
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Punishment has been hard since antiquity; deciding suits is what the Master praised.

literal: Yet what the five bureaus oversee is solely punishment and imprisonment; comparing what is heard on all sides, many discuss that the five bureaus are not refined.
idiomatic: Yet the five bureaus hold punishment alone, and reports say they are not refined.

literal: The difficulty of knowing men—how can I decide alone? I should decide together with the assembled ministers.
idiomatic: Knowing men is hard—I cannot decide alone; I shall decide with you.

literal: You each state what you have heard.”
idiomatic: Each state what you have heard."

literal: Gaozu said to Yu and Junior Director Deng Shu: “The five bureaus’ investigating officers—you take them as what grade?”
idiomatic: Gaozu asked Yu and junior director Deng Shu: "What grade for the five bureaus' investigating officers?"

literal: Yu replied: “All the investigating officers were selected by the sage’s heart.
idiomatic: Yu answered: "All were chosen by the sage's heart.

literal: In the past, when the hundred offices were first established, they were promoted as prison officials; in hearing litigation and examining statements there was no great error.
idiomatic: When offices were first set they were raised as prison officers; in hearing suits they made no great error.

literal: The reason they are second grade is that some have only just taken office, or some are slow or quick in seeing opportunity; the court already has the nine-rank system, so counting the difference of the finest thread they are made grades and ranks.
idiomatic: They are second grade because some have just taken office or differ in grasping opportunity; with the nine-rank system in place, the finest distinctions fix their grades.

literal: Taken together, what is obtained is largely similar.
idiomatic: Taken together, the results are largely alike.

literal: Gaozu said: “In recent years, because these men’s insight and views were acceptable, I selected them as prison officials; slight superiority or inferiority is not enough to make a difference.
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "I chose them for acceptable insight; slight differences are not enough to matter.

literal: Yet what the Director of the Court of Justice oversees is the root matter of human life;[7] one whose heart is level and nature upright, who restrains the strong and pities the weak, who does not avoid the noble and powerful, and who with straight feeling breaks cases—may be upper grade.
idiomatic: Yet the court of justice holds human life itself;[7] upper grade belongs to the level-hearted who restrain the strong, pity the weak, do not flinch from power, and break cases with straight feeling.

literal: Now I truly wish to listen and gather popular report; empty and full are hard to know thoroughly;
idiomatic: I wish to listen to rumor, yet truth and falsehood are hard to know;

literal: if I truly do not gather it, affairs have nothing to rest on.
idiomatic: if I do not listen, affairs have nothing to rest on.

literal: Yet those of whom people speak ill are not necessarily ill, and those of whom people speak well are not necessarily good.
idiomatic: Those called wicked are not necessarily wicked; those called good are not necessarily good.

literal: The reason is that some, in deciding litigation, do not avoid the powerful and noble, and therefore people take them for wicked;
idiomatic: Some who do not flinch from the powerful in suits are called wicked;

literal: or some restrain power and suppress the base, and the noble take them for good.
idiomatic: some who restrain power and suppress the base are praised by the noble.

literal: Yet what reaches my hearing is all the speech of the noble—therefore I hesitate and turn thrice, truly because of this.
idiomatic: Yet what reaches my ear is the noble's speech—therefore I hesitate thrice for this reason.

literal: Bureau affairs must be ice-clear and jade-pure, clearly raising praise and blame.
idiomatic: Bureau affairs must be ice-clear and jade-pure, with praise and blame made plain.

literal: You are personally in charge of the canon; wrong and right, gain and loss—you know them all in detail; you may finely distinguish and report.”
idiomatic: You personally hold the canon and know every right and wrong—distinguish finely and report."

literal: Deng Shu replied: “When Your Majesty bestows rewards and obtains the right men, the rest are content;
idiomatic: Deng Shu answered: "When rewards hit the right men, the rest are content;

literal: if rewards do not exhaust ability,[8] there is no means to encourage and urge.
idiomatic: if rewards do not reach every able man,[8] encouragement fails.

literal: In your servant’s foolish view, I wish that rewards not be carried out.”
idiomatic: In my foolish view, I wish no reward were given."

literal: Gaozu said: “In former years I established this office, promising examination of merit every three years with rewards and punishments surely carried out.
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "I established this office promising three-year examination with sure reward and punishment.

literal: Now that this examination has passed, if there is no demotion or promotion, I fear the upright will not be willing to apply their hearts and the crooked will have no means to reform and become orderly.
idiomatic: This examination has passed; without promotion or demotion the upright will not strive and the crooked will not reform.

literal: Unless one releases it to the public, how can one exhaust its utmost principle?
idiomatic: Unless judgment is public, how can principle be exhausted?

literal: Though one cannot refine its subtlest reach, I still hope for a rough palace ranking.
idiomatic: Though subtlety is beyond reach, I still want a rough ranking.

literal: Let the various Masters of Writing again with the assembled officials well measure the grounds for it.”
idiomatic: Let the Masters of Writing measure the grounds with the assembled officials."

literal: Gaozu said to the Masters of Writing and others: “I look up to continue the Qian structure and lord it over the ten thousand realms.
idiomatic: Gaozu told the Masters of Writing: "I look up to continue the Qian structure and rule the ten thousand realms.

literal: In the past I examined the ancient canon and regulations and established these hundred offices.
idiomatic: I examined ancient canon and established the hundred offices.

literal: Yet the charge of the Masters of Writing is the pivot of opportunity—not only to sum up the hundred duties and harmonize human affairs, but my gains and losses truly lie in this.
idiomatic: Yet the Masters of Writing hold the pivot—not only summing the hundred duties and harmonizing affairs, but my gains and losses lie here.

literal: From the time you have been in office, nearly two cycles have passed—you have never spoken of one fault of mine, presented one fragment of what may or may not be done, nor ever advanced one worthy or demoted one unworthy—these two matters are the greatest of crimes.”
idiomatic: Nearly two cycles you have held office without one word of my fault, one scrap of counsel, one advancement of worth or demotion of unworth—these two are your greatest crimes."

literal: Gaozu again said to Yu: “Your shallowness and thinness truly cannot compare with Jin’s great source.
idiomatic: Gaozu told Yu again: "Your shallowness cannot compare with Jin's great source.

literal: Examining the present age, the people are already beneath that.
idiomatic: In this age the people stand lower still.

literal: [9] You first became Director of the Court of Justice, and when you first became Master of Writing, inner and outer looked up—because I had a younger brother.
idiomatic: [9] When you first became director of the court of justice and then Master of Writing, court and country looked up—because you were my brother.

literal: Since last autumn’s southern banners, you have drawn near petty men and kept distant true gentlemen; in public you form factions and wound my imperial statutes; going out and coming in without rule, your movements violate ritual norms.
idiomatic: Since last autumn's march south you have drawn near petty men, kept true gentlemen distant, formed factions in public, wounded imperial law, and moved without ritual.

literal: Counting your conduct, it ought to fall in the lowest of the lower grades.”
idiomatic: By your conduct you belong in the lowest of the lower grades."

literal: Gaozu again said to Yu: “You are both younger brother at the apex of the pole and hold a post at the pivot’s end.
idiomatic: Gaozu told Yu again: "You are imperial brother at the pole's apex and hold the pivot's end.

literal: From the time you have been in office, merit and diligence in achievement have not been heard at court;
idiomatic: Since you took office no merit has been heard at court;

literal: the sound of faction repeatedly reaches my hearing.
idiomatic: faction's voice reaches me again and again.

literal: Your faults and errors have already been fully accumulated before; I cannot again narrate them separately.
idiomatic: Your faults are already fully counted; I will not list them again.

literal: Now I demote you from Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Court of Justice, but keep Special Grand Mentor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.”
idiomatic: I demote you from recorder and director of the court of justice, but leave you special grand mentor and junior tutor of the heir."

literal: He again said to Master of Writing Lu Rui: “Shufan at the beginning in the province had a very good reputation; from near times he has been partial and slack.
idiomatic: He told Master of Writing Lu Rui: "Shufan began with a fine name in office; lately he has grown partial and slack.

literal: Is it not because you and others follow his crooked and false heart and cannot guide him with righteousness—though it did not become great blame, it has already brought small punishment.
idiomatic: Is it not because you followed his crooked heart and could not guide him with righteousness—small punishment has already come.

literal: Now I strip you of one cycle of salary as Master of Writing.”
idiomatic: I strip one cycle of your salary as Master of Writing."

literal: He said to Left Vice Director Yuan Zan: “You with long-standing virtue and mature age have long held pivotal posts; you cannot gloriously support affairs of things or encourage colleagues—the saying of harming people, is it not upon you!
idiomatic: He told left vice director Yuan Zan: "You are long in virtue and age and long at the pivot, yet you cannot glorify affairs or encourage colleagues—the harm is yours!"

literal: Counting Shufan’s demotion, you ought to receive great execution—but because the blame returns to one man, I do not again blame you.
idiomatic: By Shufan's demotion you ought to face execution—but blame returns to one man and I do not punish you further.

literal: Again, as Junior Tutor, the appointment did not match what was granted; now I release you from Junior Tutor’s charge and cut one cycle of salary.”
idiomatic: As junior tutor the appointment did not match what was granted; I release you from junior tutor and cut one cycle of salary."

literal: An edict to Minister of Personnel Cui said: “Uncle is neither chief at the right nor seat at the head—how should blame be recklessly returned to the multitude’s fault?
idiomatic: He edicted Minister of Personnel Cui: "Uncle is neither chief at the right nor seat at the head—how should blame fall on the multitude?

literal: Yet observing uncle’s spirit and expression, arrogant and proud, the post of Junior Guardian seems unable to hold his intent.
idiomatic: Yet uncle's spirit is arrogant and proud; junior guardian seems beyond his intent.

literal: He may be released from Junior Guardian.”
idiomatic: Release him from junior guardian."

literal: He said to Senior Concurrent Master of Writing Yu Guo:[10] “Your career record is low and shallow; you were promoted out of turn to a famous post and cannot be diligent and cautious night and day, repeatedly pleading illness.
idiomatic: He told senior concurrent master Yu Guo:[10] "Your career is shallow; promoted out of turn you cannot be diligent night and day and repeatedly plead illness.

literal: The senior concurrent post’s rank is next below regular; now I release you from senior concurrent office—you may be Grand Master of Brilliant Virtue and Acting Master of Writing, and cut one cycle of salary.”
idiomatic: Senior concurrent rank stands next below regular; I release senior concurrent office—you may be grand master of brilliant virtue and acting master of writing, and cut one cycle of salary."

literal: He again said to Acting Master of Writing Yu Yu: “You in the Collected Documents utterly lack concern for preserving the left historian’s affairs; now I demote you to senior concurrent regular attendant and also cut one cycle of salary.”
idiomatic: He told acting master Yu Yu: "In the Collected Documents you utterly lack concern for the left historian's charge; I demote you to senior concurrent regular attendant and cut one cycle of salary."

literal: He again said to Acting Master of Writing Lu Yuan: “You first became Acting Master of Writing—it did not yet fit examining merit.
idiomatic: He told acting master Lu Yuan: "You first became acting master of writing—it did not yet fit examination.

literal: Yet you in the Collected Documents, though not of high achievement, are a literary scholar of one province; you have never taken the left historian to heart—such a fault has no place to assign blame.”
idiomatic: Yet in the Collected Documents, though not of high achievement, you are a literary man of the province; you never took the left historian to heart—such fault has nowhere to assign blame."
